title: Three steps, then you are using it.
subtitle: Look at nearby networks, save what you need on this computer, or check Bluetooth devices.
deviceHint: Connect your device to get started.
deviceStarting: Waiting for the firmware to start.
deviceReady: Your device is ready to scan.
deviceLost: The connection closed. Reconnect to continue.
scanningNote: Stop when you are ready to see the results
networkDescription: Scan nearby networks with a timed or manual stop and inspect details at a glance.
name: NETWORK
deviceRestarted: The device restarted. Waiting for it to be ready again.
emptyText: Connect your device to begin exploring.
emptyReady: Start a scan to discover nearby networks.
emptyScanning: Collecting networks. Stop the scan to see the results.
emptyNoNetworks: No networks were found. Try scanning again.
consoleDescription: Live messages and manual commands, all in one place.
unsupported: This browser does not support serial connections. Use Chrome or Edge from a local address.
startupTimeout: Still waiting for the device. Check the serial monitor, or reconnect.
listTimeout: Reading results timed out. Check the serial monitor.
portOpened: Port opened. Waiting for the device.
noResponse: Device response unconfirmed. Check the console.
functionDescription: Set the options on any card, check its command, and run it on the device.
accessoryNote: This XIAO build has no SD storage. GPS operations use an external GPS module.
resizeMonitor: Resize serial monitor with the divider or arrow keys
expandMonitor: Expand or restore serial monitor area
monitorInstructions: Drag the divider to resize · ↑ command history
sdUnavailable: This XIAO firmware build has no SD card support.
gpsRequired: Connect an external GPS module to use this operation.
streamingDescription: Output appears live in the serial monitor. Use Stop task to finish.
operationDescription: The device response appears in the serial monitor.
commandTimeout: The device did not finish responding to: {command}
busyOperation: Wait for the current operation to finish.
stopFirst: Stop the current task before starting another operation.
notConfirmed: The device did not confirm that the task started. Check the monitor or use Stop task.
partialResults: Some network details could not be retrieved. Completed results are shown.
captureDescription: Streams captured wireless frames over USB and builds a standard .pcap file in your browser (up to 32 MiB per session). Choose a target network, mode, and duration, then stop and download.
captureScope: Packet counts use the selected network. Other modes record frames on its channel.
captureNeedNetworks: Scan for networks to choose a target.
capturePartial: Capture interrupted or incomplete; complete records can be saved if available.
captureLimit: Capture reached the 32 MiB limit; saved records are available.
captureNetworkChanged: The network is no longer in the device list. Scan again.
captureSelectionFailed: The device did not confirm the network selection.
captureSettingsFailed: The device did not confirm capture settings.
captureRestoreFailed: The device did not confirm restored settings. Check device settings.
advancedDescription: Compare Wi-Fi bands, diagnose your equipment, or save a capture over USB.
commandUnavailable: Choose a command listed on the basic or advanced page.
commandNotReady: Open the command card to check its requirements or stop the current task.
wifiApScanHint: Passively listens for access point beacon frames and syncs discovered networks live to Wi-Fi results (auto-stops when the duration ends, or stop manually). Use Scan access points & stations when you need indexed device entries for selection, details, or capture.
wifiScanHint: Scans nearby access points and active associated client stations together. Automatically stops when the timer ends to load network details and station counts, or stop manually.
sniffprobeHint: Passively listens for Wi-Fi probe requests sent by nearby devices searching for networks. Prints matches live in the monitor and saves SSIDs for list -p.
sniffrawHint: Captures raw 802.11 frame statistics on the active channel in real time. Watch live activity in the serial monitor or pair with channel controls.
wifiResultsHint: Reads the access point table currently stored in device memory, including index, channel, signal, and selection state, and prints it to the monitor. Use Read device results on Wi-Fi results to sync full details into the table and dropdowns.
wifiStationsHint: Lists observed client station MAC addresses grouped under each access point along with selection status. Output appears in the serial monitor.
wifiProbesHint: Lists network names (SSIDs) recorded during probe request observation. Run probe request sniffing first and read the list in the serial monitor.
wifiInfoHint: Fetches full attributes for the selected access point, including security mode, vendor, frame count, and stations. Updates both the monitor and Wi-Fi results.
wifiSelectHint: Toggles the selected flag of the chosen access point in firmware memory (run again to unselect). Target-scoped tools such as packet counts use selected networks.
wifiClearHint: Clears stored scan results from device memory to free space for a fresh scan. Choose APs with stations or stations only, then check the confirmation box.
confirmClear: Clear this list from device memory
packetcountHint: Counts packets per second for access points and stations selected in firmware memory. Select at least one target network first and watch live rates in the monitor.
channelReadHint: Reads the device's current Wi-Fi channel setting and prints it to the serial monitor. Use this to verify which channel single-channel tasks will observe.
channelSetHint: Tunes the radio to a specific 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz Wi-Fi channel. Disable channel hopping when you want observations to stay fixed on that channel.
channelHopHint: Enables or disables automatic channel hopping across Wi-Fi channels and saves the setting on the device. Enable for broad scans, or disable to lock onto one channel.
bleScanHint: Scans nearby Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) advertisements and prints devices to the monitor. Automatically stops at the set duration to load the Bluetooth table below for CSV export.
bleResultsHint: Reads Bluetooth devices currently stored in device memory and updates the table below. Run this whenever the device is idle to inspect or export results.
stopTaskHint: Stops the active scan, detector, signal tracker, or CSI session and returns the board to idle. Automatically retrieves results after Wi-Fi or Bluetooth scans.
resyncHint: Sends a lightweight machine status probe to verify serial communication and refresh the firmware version without starting a scan.
deviceInfoHint: Reads hardware model, firmware and ESP-IDF versions, active partition, and Wi-Fi MAC addresses. Prints the full summary to the serial monitor.
deviceSettingsHint: Reads all persistent firmware settings stored on the device, such as ChanHop and SavePCAP, and prints them to the serial monitor.
resyncDone: The firmware replied. The serial connection is synchronized.
resyncFailed: The expected firmware reply did not arrive.
resyncNeedsStop: The firmware replied. Use Stop task to confirm the device is idle.
dualDescription: Sweep both bands, then open the filtered results. The previous channel-hopping setting is restored on stop.
dualScanHint: Temporarily enables channel hopping across XIAO ESP32-C5 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands. Automatically stops after the selected duration (or via the stop card) to restore ChanHop and load AP details.
dualStopHint: Stops the dual-band survey, restores the previous ChanHop setting, and loads full AP details. Click the 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz links below to view filtered results.
motionDescription: Choose your own access point and keep the board and room still for the first 30 seconds.
motionStartHint: Starts Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) motion sensing against your chosen access point. Keep the board and room still for 30 seconds to calibrate, then watch live readings below.
motionStatusHint: Queries the current CSI motion state, score, reliability, and sample rate. Updates both the reading display below and the serial monitor.
motionRecalibrateHint: Clears the active CSI baseline and starts a new 30-second still calibration without stopping the session. Run this after moving the board or altering the room.
lanDescription: Connect to your own Wi-Fi network and inspect hosts on its LAN. Check the authorization box below first: pick a scanned network or enter a Wi-Fi name and password in Connect & save Wi-Fi to store credentials on the board, then reuse Join saved Wi-Fi anytime.
wifiStatusDisconnectedHint: Connect your device to check or join a Wi-Fi network.
wifiFailedSavedDetail: Could not connect to any saved Wi-Fi profile. Check signal strength or re-enter credentials below.
wifiFailedTimeoutDetail: Timed out waiting for Wi-Fi connection ({ssid}). Check the serial monitor for details.
wifiFailedPasswordDetail: Could not connect to {ssid}. Verify the password, band, and signal strength.
wifiStatusIdleHint: Not connected to any Wi-Fi network. Authorize below and join a network before running LAN scans.
wifiStatusSyncedDisconnected: Board is currently not connected to any Wi-Fi network.
taskUnknownNote: Use Stop task or Check serial connection to confirm the board is idle.
busyNote: Waiting for the current device step to finish. Controls re-enable automatically.
lanAuthorized: I am authorized to inspect the connected network.
lanJoinPasswordHint: Choose a scanned network or enter any Wi-Fi name (SSID) and password directly to join your own access point. Successful credentials are saved on the board (up to 5 profiles) for reuse with Join saved Wi-Fi.
lanJoinAddFailed: Could not register that network name on the board. Check the SSID or serial monitor.
lanJoinDone: Connected to Wi-Fi. You can now run ARP or Ping discovery.
lanJoinDoneWithIp: Connected to {ssid} (IP {ip}). You can now run ARP or Ping discovery.
lanJoinNoSaved: No saved Wi-Fi credentials are stored on the board yet. Connect once with Connect & save Wi-Fi first.
lanJoinPasswordFailed: The device could not connect to that Wi-Fi network. Verify the password and signal, or check the serial monitor.
lanJoinHint: Joins the strongest visible Wi-Fi network matching a credential already saved on the board. If none are saved yet, connect once with Connect & save Wi-Fi first.
lanJoinFailed: The device could not join a saved Wi-Fi network. Check the monitor for details.
lanNeedWifi: Connect the board to Wi-Fi before starting ARP or Ping discovery.
lanArpHint: Sends ARP probes across the connected IPv4 subnet to discover active local-network neighbors. Stop when ready, then read the discovered host list.
lanPingHint: Sends ICMP ping checks across the connected subnet to identify hosts that respond to reachability probes. Results are stored in the device host list.
lanListHint: Reads IP addresses recorded during the most recent ARP or Ping discovery from device memory and prints them to the serial monitor.
lanStopHint: Stops the running ARP or Ping discovery scan and loads the discovered IPv4 hosts into the summary below and serial monitor.
lanHostsScanning: Scanning local hosts... Click Stop LAN scan when ready or wait for the timer.
lanHostsEmpty: No LAN hosts recorded yet. Run ARP or Ping discovery while connected to Wi-Fi.
detectorsDescription: Review broadcast types and wireless events in the serial monitor.
detectDisconnectHint: Passively listens on the active channel for 802.11 deauthentication and disassociation frames. Useful for spotting abnormal disconnect traffic in the monitor.
detectSaeHint: Passively monitors WPA3 SAE Commit authentication frames on the current channel. Prints observed handshake activity to the serial monitor.
detectPineHint: Passively watches wireless broadcasts for signatures associated with rogue hotspot tools. Any matching observations appear in the serial monitor for verification.
detectMultiHint: Passively flags a single radio or address advertising unusually many distinct SSIDs. Logs matching broadcast behavior to the serial monitor.
bleSkimmersHint: Scans nearby Bluetooth advertisements to surface serial-module names (such as HC-03, HC-05, and HC-06) commonly associated with card skimmers. Outputs findings to the monitor.
detectBluetoothHint: Passively filters Bluetooth scans for a chosen broadcast type—AirTag, iBeacon, Flock, Flipper, or Meta. Matching advertisements print live in the serial monitor.
remoteIdScanHint: Passively receives ASTM Remote ID drone broadcasts over Wi-Fi NAN and beacons, logging aircraft telemetry live to the monitor.
remoteIdListHint: Reads all Remote ID drone entries collected in device memory and prints each indexed summary to the serial monitor.
signalDescription: Choose your own access point. A reading closer to 0 dBm means a stronger signal.
signalFindWifiHint: Tracks real-time signal strength (RSSI in dBm) for the chosen access point; readings closer to 0 dBm mean a stronger signal. Move the board to help locate your hardware.
gpsReadHint: Queries one on-demand field from the external GPS module, such as fix status, satellites, coordinates, altitude, accuracy, or time, and prints it to the monitor.
gpsLiveHint: Continuously streams formatted GPS summary updates to the serial monitor. Click Stop task in the monitor when you want to stop.
gpsNmeaHint: Continuously forwards raw NMEA sentences from the external GPS module to the serial monitor for diagnosing GPS reception and message format.
stopUnconfirmed: The device did not confirm that it stopped. Check the serial monitor.
captureStationsSelected: Packet count capture requires the device station selection to be empty. Check the associated station list.
